<thought>From the measurements, all nodes lie on a single linear resistive path between terminals A and B. The resistance from A to each node gives its position along the line. By ordering the nodes by their measured resistance from A, the individual segment resistances are the differences between successive positions. This yields a series chain with the following resistors and connections:

- R1 = 6.667 Ω between A and X1  
- R2 = 5.000 Ω between X1 and N_b1  
- R3 = 10.000 Ω between N_b1 and N_b2  
- R4 = 15.000 Ω between N_b2 and N_b3  
- R5 = 20.000 Ω between N_b3 and X2  
- R6 = 5.000 Ω between X2 and N_c1  
- R7 = 10.000 Ω between N_c1 and N_c2  
- R8 = 15.000 Ω between N_c2 and N_c3  
- R9 = 20.000 Ω between N_c3 and X3  
- R10 = 10.000 Ω between X3 and N_d1  
- R11 = 15.000 Ω between N_d1 and N_d2  
- R12 = 20.000 Ω between N_d2 and B  

All measured node‑to‑node resistances are consistent with this series topology (the sum of the appropriate segment resistances equals each measured value). Therefore the inferred circuit consists of a single series chain with the above resistor values and connections.
